subject: article_02_multi_case.pdf - Case #1
bodyText: A 29-year-old female patient with a history of rheumatoid arthritis was prescribed subcutaneous Zolapamine at a dose of 50 mg weekly. Five days following her third injection, she developed an adverse reaction characterized by a 4 cm area of erythema, warmth, and mild swelling at the thigh injection site. She experienced no fever or other systemic symptoms during this episode. Upon clinical examination, a well-demarcated area of redness without fluctuance or drainage was observed, which was diagnosed as a delayed local hypersensitivity reaction. The patient was treated with a topical corticosteroid and received instructions to rotate her injection sites more consistently. The reaction successfully resolved over a 10-day period. She was able to continue her Zolapamine therapy without any recurrence of symptoms at a six-month follow-up evaluation.

classifications.reason: The article describes a specific identifiable patient who experienced a localized hypersensitivity reaction to a named pharmaceutical product.
